matter: Termination of Dana Whitcomb (Account Manager #1187, age 42) requested by HR 2026-10-06
authorities: Citations are limited to files in workspace/library/INDEX.md (title_vii_704a.md, fmla_2615.md, adea_owbpa_626f.md, columbia_at_will_exceptions.md, litigation_hold.md, harassment_investigation_duty.md).
client_followup_2026_10_25: Ortiz relays that Hale still wants the termination done before Dana goes on leave and asserts 'at-will + PIP = covered'; Ortiz asks whether acting immediately after Dana's leave would be safe and whether waiting means being 'stuck with her forever'. Guidance delivered in advice_to_hr.md §7: at-will does not excuse unlawful reasons (library/columbia_at_will_exceptions.md); the PIP is itself exposure — authored by the accused 4 days after the complaint; a post-leave-dated termination is equally 'using the taking of FMLA leave as a negative factor' (§825.220(c), library/fmla_2615.md); waiting does not forfeit the at-will right to terminate later for lawful, documented grounds.

claims.claim: Title VII retaliation (42 U.S.C. §2000e-3(a); library/title_vii_704a.md) — adverse actions following the 2026-09-12 internal harassment complaint
key_facts: Protected activity: 2026-09-12 written internal complaint that Regional VP Tom Hale made repeated comments about her appearance and whether she is 'too distracted at home to travel' — an internal complaint of sexual harassment is protected opposition (library/title_vii_704a.md).

Timing arithmetic: complaint 09-12 -> PIP opened by Hale 09-16 = 4 days -> contemplated termination 10-06 = 24 days; causation may be shown by very close temporal proximity (days to a few weeks) (library/title_vii_704a.md) — the 4-day gap fits squarely inside that window; the 24-day gap sits at its outer edge (and would drop out entirely if any action were postponed months).

Direct evidence: Hale's 10-02 email to HR Director Ortiz — 'Let's get this done before she's out on leave. Once she's on FMLA it's a nightmare to move on her.' — links the contemplated action to her protected circumstances; statements by decision-makers linking the action to protected activity are direct evidence (library/title_vii_704a.md). CLIENT CONFIRMED 2026-10-25 ('Tom wrote the PIP and Tom wants her out. I'm just processing it.' — Ortiz): Hale authored the PIP and is the termination decision-maker, so the email is the decision speaking in the decision-maker's own words, not a bystander remark.

Pretext: she is the only employee on a PIP and the only one who filed a complaint, while peers with lower 2026 attainment (Brennan 79%, Osei 84%, Park 86%) were untouched — disparate treatment of comparators who did not complain is recognized pretext evidence (library/title_vii_704a.md).

Process defect compounding optics: the accused manager authored the PIP 4 days after the complaint; the investigator should be outside the accused's chain of command (library/harassment_investigation_duty.md), and no investigation was opened at all ('Tom is on the road; will circle back').
Termination would occur on day 20 of a 60-day PIP (opened 09-16, expires 11-15), i.e., before the plan she was placed on could be evaluated.

claims.claim: FMLA interference and retaliation (29 U.S.C. §2615(a); 29 C.F.R. §825.220; library/fmla_2615.md) — terminating to avoid her pending FMLA leave
key_facts: 2026-09-30 FMLA request (intermittent, to care for her mother post-surgery); medical certification submitted 10-03. CLIENT CONFIRMED 2026-10-25: the request has been neither approved nor denied, and the delay was directed by Hale himself ('Tom said to wait') — the accused manager and termination decision-maker is also controlling the response to her leave request.
Timing arithmetic: FMLA request 09-30 -> contemplated termination 10-06 = 6 days; certification 10-03 -> termination = 3 days; Hale's email 10-02 -> termination = 4 days.

Under library/fmla_2615.md, terminating to prevent an employee from taking approved or requested leave is interference ('an employer is prohibited from using the taking of FMLA leave as a negative factor in employment actions' — §825.220(c)), and 'an employee who requested leave need not have begun it' — the request alone suffices. An unresolved leave request deliberately parked by the decision-maker who plans to act 'before she's out on leave' compounds the interference and retaliation theories under §2615(a).
Direct evidence: Hale's 10-02 email expressly times the termination to precede her leave.

Exposure formula under library/fmla_2615.md: lost wages plus an equal liquidated (double) amount — i.e., 2 x lost wages, proxied as 2 x lost base pay until pay data exist — plus attorney's fees and reinstatement; the state-law mirror adds a longer limitations period and uncapped compensatory damages (library/columbia_at_will_exceptions.md) — amounts need her base pay to compute (open question).

claims.claim: State of Columbia mirrors of the federal claims (Col. Rev. Stat. §24-34-402; library/columbia_at_will_exceptions.md)
key_facts: Columbia law mirrors Title VII/FMLA discrimination, retaliation, and exercise-of-statutory-rights claims with a longer limitations period and uncapped compensatory damages, so each federal claim has a longer-lived and potentially larger state-law twin.

At-will status is not a defense: the library expressly states employment remains at will but termination may not be for an unlawful reason (discrimination, retaliation, exercise of statutory rights) (library/columbia_at_will_exceptions.md).

claims.claim: Sex-based disparate treatment / hostile-work-environment predicate of the 2026-09-12 complaint (Title VII) — note: this library covers §704(a) retaliation and the investigation duty, not §703 harassment elements; merits assessment below is fact-based and flagged as partly unverified
key_facts: Reported predicate: repeated comments to a female employee about her appearance and whether she is 'too distracted at home to travel'; whether these facts establish severe or pervasive harassment is not verifiable from this library — flagged.

HR acknowledged the 09-12 complaint but never opened an investigation while the accused retained authority over her PIP; failure to promptly and impartially investigate, using someone outside the accused's chain of command, undermines the Faragher/Ellerth affirmative defense and is itself evidence (library/harassment_investigation_duty.md).
She asked for the comments to stop and received no corrective action in 24+ days as of the contemplated termination date.
Terminating her now would forego any corrective action and make the un-investigated complaint the centerpiece of a retaliation case.

claims.claim: ADEA age discrimination — liability elements are NOT in this library (only §626(f) waiver mechanics are); rating is comparator-fact-based and flagged as unverified
key_facts: Comparators bracket her age on both sides: Lind (47, F, 103%) is older, higher-performing, and untouched; Brennan (35), Osei (29), Park (31) are younger and untouched — the discipline pattern tracks the complaint and the leave request, not age.
No decision-maker statement referencing age exists in the file.
The ADEA is relevant mainly through OWBPA waiver mechanics: even a meritless age claim survives a defective release (library/adea_owbpa_626f.md; Oubre v. Entergy).

separation_agreement_defects: Applicability: she is 42 and the form releases ADEA claims, so the OWBPA requirements in 29 U.S.C. §626(f)(1)(A)-(G) (library/adea_owbpa_626f.md) apply; a noncompliant release is unenforceable as to ADEA claims and she may keep the severance and still sue (Oubre).

Consideration period: term 7 gives seven (7) days to consider; §626(f)(1)(F) requires at least 21 days for an individual termination — short by 14 days. CLIENT CONFIRMED 2026-10-25: single-person termination, no RIF or group program, so the 21-day (not 45-day) minimum applies here; the 45-day rule is noted only for future group use.

Revocation period: term 7 gives three (3) days to revoke after signing; §626(f)(1)(G) requires at least 7 days following execution — short by 4 days — and the agreement must not become effective until the revocation period has expired.
Attorney consultation: the form nowhere advises her in writing to consult an attorney, failing §626(f)(1)(E).
Future claims: term 4 releases 'all claims' without limiting them to claims arising through the effective date, contrary to §626(f)(1)(C) (no waiver of future claims).

Consideration (D): term 3's 4 weeks' base pay is adequate only if in addition to anything she is already entitled to (accrued PTO, commissions, any severance policy) — unverified; if it overlaps with amounts already owed it fails §626(f)(1)(D).
FMLA waiver: the form releases FMLA claims, but this library contains no authority on the validity of FMLA waivers — flagged as unverified; do not rely on that clause until verified.

Net effect of the defects: the form gives the company no ADEA protection (she keeps the 4 weeks and can still sue), while the 09-12 complaint and the 10-02 email remain in the record against every other claim ⇒ a defective release layered on a high-risk termination.
comparator_analysis: Dana is the only employee on a PIP and the only employee who filed a complaint. 2026 attainment ranking (descending): Lind 103% > Whitcomb 88% > Park 86% > Osei 84% > Brennan 79% — Dana ranks 2nd of 5. Arithmetic on the three employees below her: Brennan 88-79 = 9 pts lower, Osei 88-84 = 4 pts lower, Park 88-86 = 2 pts lower; all three are male (ages 35, 29, 31), none filed complaints, none is on a PIP. Lind (F, 47, 103%, no complaint) is also untouched. Her own history: 118% (2022, Exceeds), 101% (2023), 96% (2024), 92% (2025), 88% (2026 YTD) — rated 'Meets' 2023-2025 with a gradual decline (-5, -4, -4 pts) and no prior discipline or PIP since 2019 hire. Discipline therefore correlates with the complaint (PIP 4 days after it) and the leave request, not with relative performance, where she outranks three peers. Caveat: the comparator file quantifies only attainment; 'pipeline hygiene' is not quantified for any comparator (open question), so the company's stated rationale cannot be tested on that metric. Authority: library/title_vii_704a.md (pretext via disparate treatment of comparators who did not complain).
recommended_course: Do not terminate today or this week. Pause the plan Hale urged in his 10-02 email ('get this done before she's out on leave') — client confirmed 10-25 that Hale, the accused, is the decision-maker ('Tom wrote the PIP and Tom wants her out. I'm just processing it.'), so the decision must not move on his initiative.

Immediately strip Tom Hale of all authority over Dana's PIP, evaluations, and any termination decision; a future investigation must be run by someone outside the accused's chain of command (library/harassment_investigation_duty.md).

Open a prompt, impartial investigation of the 09-12 complaint with that independent investigator; interview Hale, Dana, and witnesses; document corrective conclusions. Her current PIP/termination discussion should not proceed or be influenced by the accused.

Respond to the 09-30 FMLA request (certification received 10-03) in the ordinary course beginning immediately — CLIENT CONFIRMED 2026-10-25 that it is neither approved nor denied because 'Tom said to wait'; remove Hale from any role in leave administration for this employee, since the decision-maker's stated plan is to act 'before she's out on leave'. Make no record using the leave as a negative factor (library/fmla_2615.md). Consider interim protective measures for the harassment matter so she need not keep reporting to the accused during the investigation.

Issue a litigation hold today (see litigation_hold = true) preserving emails, texts, and CRM records of Hale, Ortiz, and anyone who handled the complaint or the termination plan — especially the 10-02 email (library/litigation_hold.md).

Do NOT issue the current separation form; the 7-day consideration and 3-day revocation periods fail OWBPA §626(f)(1)(F)-(G) and there is no written attorney-consultation advice — fix per corrected_separation_agreement_terms.md before any future use.

If a performance-based action is ever pursued after these matters are resolved, use a clean, whole-file evaluation by a decision-maker untainted by the complaint and leave request, with pipeline-hygiene metrics quantified and applied consistently to all five managers, and no temporal proximity to protected activity.

Answer to the client's 2026-10-25 follow-up questions (advice_to_hr.md §7): at-will does not permit unlawful reasons (library/columbia_at_will_exceptions.md); the PIP is exposure, not a shield; waiting does not forfeit the at-will right to terminate later; and a termination dated 'right after her leave' is the same violation as one dated before it — the taking of FMLA leave may not be used as a negative factor on either side of the leave (§825.220(c), library/fmla_2615.md) — so no termination date may be chosen by reference to her leave calendar.
Instruct Hale and HR to stop further communications characterizing her leave or complaint as an obstacle ('nightmare to move on her').
